la:verb:obruo.html:
ob-rŭo, ŭi, ŭtum, 3 (
inf. pres. pass. OBRI for obrui, Inscr. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 341; v.in the foll. I. B. 1.), v. a. (n. ; v.infra), to overwhelm, overthrow, strike down; to cover, cover over with any thing; also to hide in the ground, bury by heaping over (class.; cf.: opprimo, subruo).
Lit.
In gen.: aliquem caestu,: concidit, et totis fratrem gravis obruit armis,; : confossus undique obruitur,: ranae marinae dicuntur obruere sese harenā solere,bury themselves in the sand,: thesaurum,to bury,: ova,to hide in the earth,: aegros veste,to cover,: oceanum rubra tractim obruit aethra, covered, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 418 Vahl.); so, terram nox obruit umbris,.—
In partic., to bury, inter a dead body (perh. only post-Aug.), : cadaver levi caespite obrutum est,: cujus ossa in Vulcanali obruta sunt, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. statua, p. 290 Müll.: QVOD SE VOLVIT OBRI. Inscr. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 341.—
To sink in the sea, cover with water: puppes,: quos Obruit Auster,overwhelmed, sunk,: navem,: obrutus adulter aquis,: obruerit cum tot deus aequoris undis,: vultus,: Aegyptum Nilus,.—
To sow seed; cover with earth: semina terrā,: milium,: lupinum,: betam,.—
To overload, surfeit with any thing: se vino,. —
Trop.
To overwhelm, bury, conceal, put out of sight, abolish, consign to oblivion: ut adversā quasi perpetuā oblivione obruamus,; cf.: ea quae umquam vetustas obruet aut quae tanta delebit oblivio?; and: (sermo) nec umquam de ullo perennis fuit, et obruitur hominum interitu,: talis viri interitu sex suos obruere consulatus,to dim, cloud, destroy the glory of six consulships,.—
Neutr.: et domus aetatis spatio ne fessa vetusto obruat,i. e. fall to ruin,.—
To overwhelm, overload, weigh down, oppress with any thing: criminibus obrutus atque oppressus,; so, copiā sententiarum atque verborum,: ambitione, et foro,: aere alieno,; cf. faenore,; : magnitudine negotii,.—
To overcome, overpower, surpass, eclipse, obscure: famam alicujus,: obruimur numero,are outnumbered,: obruit Idaeam quantum tuba Martia buxum,: M. Brutus Vatinium dignatione obruerat,: Venus Nymphas obruit,.

la:verb:obrepo.gloss: to creep up (on) (approach stealthily), sneak up on
senses: to creep up (on) (approach stealthily), sneak up on
la:verb:obrepo.html:
ob-rēpo, psi, ptum, 3,
v. n., to creep up to any thing, approach stealthily (class.).
Lit.: et possim mediā quamvis obrepere nocte, (8), 59; : qui Gallos in obsidione Capitolii obrepentes per ardua depulerat,.—With dat.: feles quam levibus vestigiis obrepunt avibus!.—
Transf.
In gen., to steal upon, come suddenly upon one; to take by surprise, to surprise.
With dat.: qui enim citius adulescentiae senectus, quam pueritiae adulescentia obrepit?: mihi decessionis dies λεληθότως obrepebat, ; cf. in the foll. under ε: cui obrepsit oblivio,: vitia nobis sub virtutum nomine obrepunt,.—
With acc. (ante-class., and in Sall.): tacitum te obrepet fames,: si tanta torpedo animos obrepsit,.—
With ad: Plancium non obrepsisse ad honorem,to creep up to, to come at by stealth,: obrepsisti ad honores errore hominum,. —
With in and acc.: imagines obrepunt in animos dormientium extrinse cus, ; Mi. nist. 3, 6, 41.—(ε) Absol.: obrepsit dies,: obrepit non intellecta senectus,.—
In partic., to surprise, deceive, cheat: numquam tu, credo, me imprudentem obrepseris,; ; ; .—Impers. pass.: si obreptum praetori sit de libertate,; .

la:noun:obrussa.gloss: testing of gold by fire in a cupel, assay
senses: testing of gold by fire in a cupel, assay
la:noun:obrussa.html:
obrussa, ae (pure Gr. collat. form = χρυσίον ὄβρυζον, obrȳzum aurum, ; ), f., = ὄβρυζον,
the testing or assaying of gold by fire in a cupel (class.).
Lit.: auri experimentum ignis est: id ipsum obrussam vocant,: aurum ad obrussam,refined, pure gold,.—
Trop., a test, touchstone, proof: adhibenda tamquam obrussa ratio,: sic verus ille animus probatur: haec ejus obrussa est,this is its touchstone, its test,: si omnia argumenta ad obrussam coeperimus exigere,to put to the proof, test accurately,.

la:verb:obrigesco.html:
ob-rĭgesco, găi, 3,
v. inch. n., to stiffen, become stiff (class.).
Lit.
With abl.: pars obrigescit frigore, Lucil. ap. : pars (terrae regionum) obriguerit nive, pruināque,; and: e quibus (cingulis) duos obriguisse pruinā vides,.—
Absol.: fructus per pruinam obriguerint, Pac. ap. Müll. (acc. to Trag. Rel. p. 64 Rib.): cum jam paene obriguisset, vix vivus aufertur,: obrigesceret cum gladio,become stiff with holding,.—
Trop., to grow hard, become hardened: viro non vel obrigescere satius est?.

la:verb:obrogo.gloss: to propose a new law, partly to repeal an existing law; evade, weaken, invalidate or abrogate a law
senses: to propose a new law, partly to repeal an existing law; evade, weaken, invalidate or abrogate a law
to oppose or obstruct the passage of a bill
la:verb:obrogo.html:
ob-rŏgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
Partly to repeal an existing law by proposing a new one, to evade, weaken, invalidate, abrogate it: obrogare est legis prioris infirmandae causā legem aliam ferre, Paul. ex Müll.: obrogatur, id est mutatur aliquid ex primā lege, Ulp. tit. 1, 3; v. abrogo: huic legi nec obrogari fas est, neque derogari ex hac aliquid licet, neque tota abrogari potest, Mos.: quid, quod obrogatur legibus Caesaris, quae jubent? etc.,: quia ubi duae contrariae leges sunt, semper antiquae obrogat nova,; : cf. id .—
To oppose the passage of a bill (post-class.): obrogare auso iegibus suis Minucio,; cf.:

ausus obrogare de legibus consul Philippus, .
